projects.name: Sport — Multi-Agent AI Operations System
projects.tagline: A Chief-of-Staff AI that coordinates venture CEOs and specialist agents across every project.
projects.writeup: Sport is the operating system for a portfolio of AI ventures. It runs a hierarchy of agents — an executive coordinator, venture CEOs, and specialists — over a shared kanban/task bus, with approval gates on anything that leaves the machine. Built to remove the human bottleneck from repetitive operations: monitoring, research, drafting, and reporting all run as scheduled agent jobs.
highlights: Multi-agent orchestration with role hierarchy and task routing
Approval-gated outbound actions (nothing posts or sends without sign-off)
Scheduled autonomous jobs + realtime status dashboard

projects.name: Smart Home Hub — Home Assistant on a Raspberry Pi
projects.tagline: Type what you want your house to do in plain English; a scheduled agent writes, validates and deploys the real Home Assistant automation.
projects.writeup: A Raspberry Pi 5 running Home Assistant in Docker, with Mosquitto and ESPHome alongside it, reachable over a private tailnet instead of the public internet — the house is never exposed. On top of it sits a plain-English automation builder: describe the automation you want in one sentence, from a text box on the dashboard or by voice, and a scheduled agent picks it up, writes the real Home Assistant automation, validates it through the config API, reloads the config, and writes the outcome back to the dashboard. The chain is event-driven and silent when idle, so it costs nothing until there is something to build. A nightly job mirrors the Home Assistant configuration to a second machine and the restore drill has been run, so a bad automation cannot take the house down.
highlights: Plain-English to working automation: type or speak a request and a scheduled agent writes, validates and deploys it, then reports the result back
Custom dashboard rather than the stock overview — the builder, the live automation list, hub health and backup status on one page, served over a private tailnet and never the public internet
Nightly configuration mirror to a second machine with a tested restore path
Running today: morning weather and sunrise briefing, shopping-list reminder, a left-on watchdog for the media player, and an automatic-backup staleness alert

projects.name: Token Killers — LLM Cost Optimization
projects.tagline: A measurable service that cuts AI API spend by re-architecting prompts, context, and routing.
projects.writeup: Token Killers is an audit-and-rebuild service for teams bleeding money on AI APIs. It combines prompt/context compression, model routing, caching, and local-model offload — then proves the savings with a before/after calculator. The differentiator is that I run the same stack on my own hardware, so the claims are verifiable, not theoretical.
highlights: Interactive savings calculator (public lead magnet)
Local-LLM offload for privacy + zero marginal cost
Playbook productized as a paid PDF

projects.name: Gold Spot Explorer
projects.tagline: Ranks historical gold ground against where you actually find it — then reads USGS bare-earth LiDAR to pick out the creek beds and ravines themselves and score which one is your source.
projects.writeup: Gold Spot Explorer is one of the systems in my AI portfolio. Ranks historical gold ground against where you actually find it — then reads USGS bare-earth LiDAR to pick out the creek beds and ravines themselves and score which one is your source. Overlays active BLM claims, private property lines and public streams, and re-renders the terrain at every zoom so old diggings stay readable close in. A 3D button lifts the map into a real elevation mesh you can tilt, spin and exaggerate — every overlay drapes onto the actual ground, so a bench or a creek bed reads as real relief instead of a flat outline. Tells you whether ground is claimed, BLM, National Forest, state or private — and shades the public land on every basemap and at every zoom, in a custom overlay where green means federal ground you can generally stake a claim on and red means federal ground closed to mineral entry, so you know at a glance whether you may mine before you drive out. Includes a free AI guide that runs on this machine — ask it about the ground on screen and it points the map at its answer. Scores 0–100, walkable target zones, satellite + terrain overlay, GPX export. Free public data.
highlights: Ranks historical gold ground against where you actually find it — then reads USGS bare-earth LiDAR to pick out the creek beds and ravines themselves and score which one is your source.
